chains.trait: Complex, mournful vocal harmonies from throat sac
links: Dense atmosphere and temperature inversions allow sound to carry miles
K2V stable light cycle and prairie openness favor auditory communication
Herds maintain cohesion and mourn loss via long-range acoustic signals
Qu-gene locks preserve neural architecture for complex vocal processing

skill.effect: The Mantelope sings a sorrowful harmony that pacifies nearby kin and forces hidden adversaries to reveal themselves.

chains.weakness: Attracts predators; song stops if vocal cords are damaged.
observe: Throat sac inflates to resonance frequency
Herds gather and hum in dissonant harmony
Ears twitch toward distant echoes of their own calls

journal.en: A library of song trapped in a grazer's throat; they sing the history of a people they can no longer remember.

plausibility.summary: Describe as long-duration, low-frequency chorus with formant shifts from an inflated laryngeal air sac (individuals overlap calls), not intentional multipart harmony; cap effective "reveal" range at hundreds of metres only downwind/in inversion conditions, not miles every night.
fixes: Describe as long-duration, low-frequency chorus with formant shifts from an inflated laryngeal air sac (individuals overlap calls), not intentional multipart harmony; cap effective "reveal" range at hundreds of metres only downwind/in inversion conditions, not miles every night.

analogues.organism: Howler monkey (Alouatta) hyoid/throat amplification for long-range low calls; sage-grouse (Centrocercus) inflatable esophageal air sacs for display vocals.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Human neural architecture in quadrupedal grazer frame
links: Qu grafted synthetic proteins preserve encephalic volume
Sterile plains remove predation pressure to prune unused tissue
15°C climate traps cranial heat, imposing metabolic tax
Caloric deficit selects against brain mass over time

skill.effect: Use a Mantelope to solve puzzles or decode Qu ruins; grants insight into past civilizations.

chains.weakness: Suffers overheating in direct sun; must rest in shade or risk heat stroke.
observe: Large eyes dart with confusion between quad movement and mental tasks
Calves with smaller heads graze faster and reach maturity sooner
Adults lie listless, conserving energy for neural maintenance

journal.en: The world falls silent not because the singers are gone, but because the half-minded grow faster.

plausibility.summary: Add explicit heat-dissipation limiter (no elephantine pinnae): shade-rest mechanic is required; selection gradient on calf head size should be fast (10²–10³ generations), not subtle.
fixes: Add explicit heat-dissipation limiter (no elephantine pinnae): shade-rest mechanic is required; selection gradient on calf head size should be fast (10²–10³ generations), not subtle.

analogues.organism: Island/rule and feral ungulate brain shrinkage; philosophical analogue to locked-in cognition without motor affordance (clinical locked-in syndrome—conceptual only).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

relations.note: Divergent neural retention; Mantelopes retain human encephalic volume at high metabolic cost, while prey prune neural tissue for faster grazing and survival.
Titan low-frequency booms mask Mantelope mournful harmonies, disrupting herd communication and acoustic cohesion across the prairie.
Hand Flappers mimic Mantelope mournful harmonies to infiltrate herds and steal grazing time, exploiting acoustic overlap in dense air.
